title: The Kitchen
architect_intro: Kitchen. Eleven at night. One bulb. Your uncle has been here since nine.
player_goal: Hemant's signature on the guarantor form, and his last three bank statements, by Friday.
stated_objection: The bank people want so many papers. Let me ask my CA.

hidden_objection_layers.text: The shop account is overdrawn and his sister does not know.

objects.label: Gas agency calendar
objects.reveals_text: Turned to last month. He has stopped looking at dates.

objects.label: Bank form by the onions
objects.reveals_text: Unsigned. Section 4, 'Applicant's guarantor: bank statements (3 months)', has been circled in pencil, hard enough to tear.

k1.speaker: hemant_joshi
k1.line: Arre, come, come. Sit. You've eaten? There's poha from morning. I'll heat it.

tells.reading: He's busying his hands so he doesn't have to look at you.
tells.false_positive: Habit. He dries things when he talks. He always has.

choices.text: I've eaten, Mama. I came about the bank form.
Poha would be nice. How's the shop been?
Mama, the form's due Friday. If it's not in, I lose the seat.

k2.speaker: hemant_joshi
k2.line: Haan, haan, the form. One minute. These bank people, they want so many papers. Let me ask my CA once. After this week.

tells.reading: A stall with no reason attached.
tells.false_positive: Real caution. Guarantor papers are serious. Asking a CA is sensible.

choices.text: Which papers are worrying you?
It's only three statements. Ten minutes at the branch. I'll come with you.

rebuttal.text: Ten minutes, ten minutes. You don't know these branch people. Half a day, minimum.

choices.text: Aai already said you'd do it. She'll be hurt if you back out now.
[say nothing]

k3.speaker: hemant_joshi
k3.line: Shop is shop. Exam season is good, then nothing. Everybody has phones now, who photocopies? You know, I still walk Parvati every morning. A hundred and three steps to the first landing. I don't miss.

tells.reading: He answered the shop question with the hill.
tells.false_positive: He just likes talking about the hill. He tells everyone the number.

choices.text: A hundred and three. Even in the rains?
You said 'then nothing'. Is the shop okay?
Good. So, the bank form.

k3b.speaker: hemant_joshi
k3b.line: Rains, Covid, your cousin's wedding. Covid time I went at five so no police. [He laughs.] The bank manager has a moustache like the hill, you know. Steps all the way. [He stops.] Sorry. That wasn't funny. I'm tired.

choices.text: You're allowed to be tired, Mama. What's going on?
It was a bit funny. Shall we look at the form together?

line_by_state.line: [Long pause. He puts the tumbler down.] Statements. Hemu, you fool. The current account is, it's in minus. Since Diwali last year. Your Aai doesn't know. If the bank sees, they'll say no, and then everybody will know.
Nothing is worrying me. Just these bank people. Leave it with me.

tells.reading: His mother's name for him. He's ashamed.
tells.false_positive: It's just how he talks to himself.

choices.text: Thank you for telling me. The bank takes a fixed-deposit lien instead of statements. I checked. Can we go Saturday, together?
I won't tell Aai. And if you'd rather not sign, I'll ask someone else. No hard feelings.
Okay. Can I ask something else, then. What would make Friday easier for you?
Mama, I need it by Friday. Please just sign.
If you don't sign, I'll have to tell Aai why.

k5.speaker: hemant_joshi
k5.line: [He waves the dishcloth.] And then they'll want the shop papers also. Then GST. Then what. [He doesn't finish.]
k5.note: Weak rebuttal: certainty drops; next truthful move gets x1.5.

tells.reading: He's afraid of what the papers will show.
tells.false_positive: He hates paperwork. Most shopkeepers do.

choices.text: Then what, Mama?
They won't want GST. I'll handle the rest. Sign tonight and I'll do the running.

k6.speaker: hemant_joshi
k6.line: FD lien. [He thinks.] I have the FD from your Aaji's gold, forty thousand. That's enough? [He picks up the pen, puts it down.] Saturday. I'll wear the good shirt. These branch people respect a good shirt.

choices.text: The good shirt. Ten o'clock?
Sign now, so it's done?

k7.speaker: hemant_joshi
k7.line: No, no. Who else will you ask. [He laughs, short.] I'll sign. Tell me how to do it without the statements.

choices.text: The bank takes an FD lien. Saturday, together. I'll come.

line_by_state.line: [He puts the tumbler down hard.] I said I'll see. Diwali is coming, everything is busy. After Diwali.
Okay, okay. Give the pen. [He signs. He doesn't look at you.] Statements I'll send.

choices.text: Okay, Mama. After Diwali.
Thank you, Mama.

k9.speaker: hemant_joshi
k9.line: [Pause. He takes the pen.] Fine. Fine. Where. [He signs fast.] Go now, it's late. Your Aai will worry.

choices.text: Thanks, Mama.

end_clean.architect: He was at the branch before you on Saturday. Room closed.

end_clean_hasty.architect: He signed by the onions. Room closed.

end_dark.architect: You got a yes. You did not get an agreement. He will remember the difference before you do.

afterword.speaker: hemant_joshi
afterword.clean: The child is sensible, Shobha. Came with me to the bank. Like a grown-up.
afterword.partial: I signed. What more do they want from me.
afterword.dark: Your child talks like a lawyer now.
afterword.loss: They were in a hurry. Everyone is in a hurry.
